Key specs - Sizes: XXS to XXL - Material: 100% cotton - Colors: three A dressed-up, lightweight cotton-silk polo: Suitsupply Long Sleeve Polo Top pick With its slim fit and drapey cotton-silk fabric, this elevated long-sleeve polo can take you from the office to date night. It’s extra lightweight, though, so it may not work when the temperature drops. The Suitsupply Long Sleeve Polo is the kind of well-rounded, supremely useful garment that can be worn straight from work to dinner at a nice restaurant. Made from a smooth, drapey blend of cotton and silk — with refined details, like mother-of-pearl buttons — this option splits the difference between a slim-fit lightweight sweater and a dress shirt in the best possible way. This lightweight sweater is slim and refined. The Long Sleeve Polo has an elegant, European feel. It’s slim through the chest and shoulders, so if you prefer a roomier fit, you may need to size up. I’m 6-foot-3, and the size L was long enough for me to tuck into pants with a higher waist, but with jeans it could have been tricky. However, this polo has fine ribbing on the (slightly oversize) collar, cuffs, and waist, and the ribbed hem (which hits around the belt line) gives the shirt a polished look, even when it’s untucked. The neckline opens wider than those of other polos we tested, and there are four mother-of-pearl buttons on the placket. You can do up two or three buttons for a more conservative look, or you can leave all but one unbuttoned (my preference) for a look that’s a little more louche. The Long Sleeve Polo comes in around four colors (which vary seasonally), and the Dark Brown and Sand shades we tested were a little more interesting than the Navy and Black options. (Note: Suitsupply also makes this polo in a short-sleeve version, and it comes in 14 colors. We haven’t tested it, but it’s made from the same material as the version we tried, and it’s likely to be just as appealing.) It’s dressy, yet not overly so. This pick nails a particular sweet spot: It offers the sharpness of a sweater-and-collared-shirt combo without any of the formality. “This is by far the best-looking shirt of the bunch,” one tester said. “It works dressed up or down.” It pairs equally well with jeans, chinos, and clothing with lightweight tailoring — you could genuinely wear this polo with a suit. The fabric is a drapey blend of 70% cotton and 30% silk. The material has a subtle sophistication, which sets this pick apart. The texture is smooth and slightly shiny, and that fits the tailored vibe. “This is an exceptionally soft shirt — it feels luxe and high quality,” remarked a tester. “There’s a great mix of style and comfort.” Though the material isn’t as airy as pure silk, it’s still very lightweight and breathable; this polo can definitely work in the summer. And if you want additional warmth or coverage, it could be worn with an undershirt, since the fabric is thin. (For what it’s worth, I hate the look of a crewneck under a polo, so I’d wear a tank top under it, for comfort and warmth, and to disguise any nipple visibility.) Flaws but not dealbreakers The slim fit may not work for everyone. This shirt’s (intentionally) trim cut is body-skimming. Consider sizing up if you prefer more room. The cotton-silk blend requires some TLC. To keep the fabric looking good (and to avoid shrinkage), the Long Sleeve Polo should be washed on a cold, delicate cycle and air-dried. Key specs - Sizes: XS to XXL - Materials: 70% cotton, 30% silk - Colors: three A polished, extra-soft sweater: Charles Tyrwhitt Pure Merino Knitted Polo Top pick This lightweight polo sweater is made of extra-soft, machine-washable merino wool. Considering the quality, this one is well priced, and it goes on sale often. But we wish it came in a (lighter, brighter) selection of colors. The Charles Tyrwhitt Pure Merino Knitted Polo is the kind of garment that grows on you. Made from a fine merino wool that’s incredibly soft from the start, this polo sweater gets even softer with time as you wash it (in a machine!) and wear it. The wool is very soft and gets better over time. The Pure Merino Knitted Polo is made from 100% merino wool that’s Woolmark-certified — a mark of durability, performance, and quality. It’s been garment-washed, which means it’s been treated to prevent shrinkage and to make it softer, and this is indeed one of the softest pieces we tested. I found the sweater notably comfortable from the first wear (the company says it molds to your body over time, but I haven’t tested it for long enough to confirm that). And it’s not the least bit itchy. Another bonus: It’s machine-washable. (Our other merino picks call for hand-washing or dry-cleaning, though our laundry experts insist that you can machine-wash most wool, as long as you use cold water and a gentle cycle.) This is a plus for those who want to wear knit polos but are worried they’ll have to baby these items. It’s temperature-regulating and odor-resistant. Although this polo sweater is notably thicker than our cotton-silk Suitsupply Long Sleeve Polo pick, it’s just as breathable. The insulating merino fibers keep you cool or warm, as needed: I found this piece ideal for days when the weather couldn’t make up its mind. And merino wool is also odor-resistant; I wore this shirt on a day that hit 74 degrees Fahrenheit, and there were no unpleasant odors. Because it is temperature-regulating — and wrinkle-resistant — this garment is particularly good for travel and transitional weather. It’s our most office-friendly pick. This polo sweater is just as professional as a dress shirt, but it has more personality. (And, in my opinion, it also looks far more expensive than it is.) The collar, cuffs, and hem have a ribbed finish, and it has a three-button placket, so you can create more breathing room at the neck if you unbutton two or three buttons. The fit is trim (though not slim), and it comes in sizes from XS to XXXL. The cut falls in between the slim Suitsupply Long Sleeve Polo pick and the roomier, more classic fit of the Polo Ralph Lauren Mesh Long-Sleeve Polo Shirt. The hem sits right around the belt line; this top looks fine tucked into high-waisted pants or left untucked with jeans or casual pants. Flaws but not dealbreakers More color options would be nice. This polo comes in five colors, but four of them are quite dark (Black, Charcoal, Forest Green, and Navy), with just one light color (Cream). Key specs - Sizes: XS to XXXL - Materials: merino wool - Colors: five An upscale merino sweater that wears like a sweatshirt: AYR The Two-a-Days Top pick This stylish crewneck sweater has an easy, relaxed fit with angled raglan sleeves; it’s made from high-end merino wool that’s breathable but also has a nice bit of heft. At nearly $300, it’s our priciest pick, and it comes in only two colors. What do you get when you combine raglan sleeves with fine merino wool? AYR’s The Two-a-Days, a comfortable, elevated sweater that moves effortlessly between casual and smart. A raglan sleeve extends in one piece continuously from the cuff to the neckline, with diagonal seams running from the underarm to the collarbone. This design is most often associated with classic terry sweatshirts and baseball shirts, and it creates a relaxed, sporty look. But here it’s paired with luxurious merino wool and dark, moody colorways, and the result is an unexpectedly elegant sweater that can be dressed up or down. The material is extra breathable. The AYR Two-a-Days is made from 100% extra-fine merino wool, which is highly breathable, thanks to its crimped fiber structure (small air pockets that insulate while allowing moisture to escape). This is true of all merino, but temperature regulation is even greater with this sweater because of its relatively loose weave. In terms of weight, it has a nice heft to it, especially compared with our other merino pick, the Banana Republic Merino Crew-Neck Sweater. But it doesn’t feel heavy or hot; I wore it on one of those April days when the temperature swung from 44 to 70 degrees, and the sweater remained comfortable at both extremes. Breathability isn’t the only benefit of this wool. This sweater’s extra-fine merino wool — sourced from a heritage Italian mill — has a noticeably softer hand than most wool knits at this price. Like all merino, it’s antimicrobial and odor-resistant. (I can attest that it didn’t pick up any underarm odor after multiple wears without washing.) And it resists wrinkles well enough that I could pull it straight from a suitcase and wear it without having to steam it. All of this makes the sweater a natural for commuting, traveling, and working in an office. Compared with our Banana Republic Merino Crew-Neck sweater pick (which is around $185 less), this sweater is thicker, more durable, totally itch-free, and just as soft against the skin. We love its distinctive silhouette. Of all our sweater picks, this one has the sportiest silhouette — raglan sleeves, a high ribbed crewneck, and a relatively short, ribbed hem that nods to classic athletic wear (hence the name, a reference to two-a-day practices). Despite the sporty DNA, it has a clean, regular fit. So it works over a tee, under a jacket, and with just about anything on the bottom: jeans, chinos, trousers, even sweatpants or shorts. But there are limitations: It’s a bit too casual to wear under a blazer or sport coat. Flaws but not dealbreakers It’s pricey. At $275, it’s the most expensive of our picks. It’s hand-wash-only. And you hang it to dry. That isn’t unusual for merino wool, but it’s a consideration for people who prefer the convenience of machine-washable garments. Key specs - Sizes: XS to XXLL - Material: 100% merino wool - Colors: three A budget-friendly basic: Banana Republic Merino Crew-Neck Sweater Top pick Made from thin, lightweight merino wool, this simple crewneck comes in over a dozen colors and in two fits. (We recommend sizing up.) It’s well priced, but it does feel flimsy compared with our pricier merino-wool picks. Every closet needs a sweater like this one: a stylish, in-between-seasons basic that works on its own or layered — and not so pricey that you have to be precious with it. At around $90 (and sometimes much less, during frequent sales), the lightweight Banana Republic Merino Crew-Neck Sweater offers great value. It feels soft against the skin, and it comes in sizes and cuts that work for lots of different bodies. This is surprisingly good-quality wool for the price. This sweater is made from 100% extra-fine merino wool, a wool type that offers good temperature regulation and a softer, less-itchy feel than regular wool. Banana Republic’s wool is produced under the NATIVA protocol, a certification that ensures it’s traceable, sustainably sourced, and ethically produced. Considering the price, we were pleasantly surprised by how good this sweater felt. “The material was nice and light — a little scratchy, but overall pretty soft for wool,” according to one tester. That said, the sweater is thin — the thinnest of our merino wool picks, by far — and the fabric feels somewhat flimsy when it’s rubbed between two fingers. We’re okay with that, though, again considering the price. Plus, this is the definition of a lightweight layer. It is a classic crewneck with a straight fit, but it runs small. The Merino Crew-Neck has a straight cut; it’s not intended to be slim. However, it runs fairly small, so consider sizing up. I’m 6-foot-3, and I tested it in a size L; there was enough room for a (very) thin undershirt, but an XL would’ve given me more breathing room. The Regular fit comes in sizes XS to XXL, and the Tall fit comes in sizes M to XXL, if you need more length in the torso. The sweater’s hem, cuffs, and crewneck are finely ribbed, but otherwise there’s no extra detailing. Because this one is such a blank canvas, it makes an excellent layering piece, worn over a dress shirt or under a light jacket. Flaws but not dealbreakers It’s not the most low-maintenance option. To keep this sweater looking good, follow the care label: Hand-wash it in cold water and air-dry it flat, or dry-clean it. Don’t make the same mistake I did and throw it in the washing machine on a regular wash cycle: The sweater shrank about an inch all around. (Vigorous friction from the washing machine causes wool fibers to contract.) I was able to gently stretch the sweater back out after rewashing it, but I don’t recommend this route. It runs small. If you’re on the fence or need room for layering, go up a size. While this sweater is nice for the price, the merino wool is extremely thin. We’re also skeptical about how it’ll age: “There was a tiny bit of fuzziness visible on the fabric, and I can imagine this might pill,” one tester said. Key specs - Sizes: XS to XXL, XS to XXL (Regular), M to XXL (Tall) - Materials: 100% merino wool - Colors: six A chunky yet lightweight cotton crewneck: Alex Crane Bay Sweater Top pick This relaxed, sharp-looking crewneck is very comfortable. It’s made from high-quality ribbed cotton that’s chunky yet surprisingly light, but the loose weave means it can snag fairly easily. If your wardrobe could use one excellent cotton sweater that ticks the most important boxes — incredibly comfortable, stylish, and versatile — consider splurging for the Alex Crane Bay Sweater. Among our sweater picks, this ribbed option is my overall favorite, and though it looks chunky, it’s actually remarkably lightweight, breathable, and delightful to wear. It has a relaxed fit, and it comes in several versatile core and seasonal colors. This is a wear-it-all-the-time option. And I’ve done just that: The Bay Sweater pairs easily with jeans, chinos, fatigues, and even pleated trousers, for a relaxed-yet-polished look. The chunky knit is reminiscent of vintage fisherman sweaters, and even though it’s made from cotton, it has the softness and texture of a super-high-quality wool. This sweater is incredibly comfy and breathable, so it’s perfect for early spring, when the temperature swings a lot. I tested the Ink colorway (a faded black that’s incredibly versatile and just different enough to be interesting). And it comes in other appealing shades, such as Coffee and Bone.) The classic cut fits just right. The sweater has a roomy, relaxed fit, but it’s not baggy or long. It’s roomy enough to wear a collared shirt underneath, or you could wear the sweater under a spring jacket. (You wouldn’t want to wear it under a blazer or a snug denim jacket, though; it’s a bit too bulky for that.) The neck is roomy yet not too loose, and the sleeves and hem are ribbed. It looks chunky, but it’s surprisingly light. The Bay Sweater is made with high-quality, luxe-feeling cotton from India. And it’s the chunkiest of our picks, yet it’s still lightweight: This sweater is loosely woven, so it’s cooler and more breathable than wool but still provides texture and warmth. It’s comfortable enough that I found myself reaching for it at home, yet it’s polished enough that I wanted to wear it out. A warning, however: Because this sweater has a loose, fairly open weave, it did snag a bit on occasion. A few threads came loose, and I had to pull them through the garment to hide them. When I was wearing it while doing chores, for example, the sweater snagged on a sliver of wood in our stairwell. It wasn’t a huge issue, though, and it didn’t change my feelings about the sweater. You can just toss it in the wash. The Bay Sweater is machine-washable (on cold). It didn’t shrink at all when I washed it, though I didn’t put it in the dryer. But, as with any cotton item, there’s a chance it could shrink. Flaws but not dealbreakers It’s expensive for a cotton sweater. But the quality is very apparent. Snagging might be an issue. The ribbed, loose knit easily catches on things (as I found out when I was testing it). Key specs - Sizes: XS to XXL - Materials: 100% organic cotton - Colors: five (four core, one seasonal) A classic style for layering: J.Crew Heritage Cotton Quarter-Zip Sweater Top pick A fresh-feeling take on the classic quarter-zip, this sweater comes in vibrant colors, has a collar that holds its shape, and is made from soft cotton that’s substantial without being heavy. It works well for most seasons, but it’s too thick for summer. The quarter-zip sweater could be undergoing a style renaissance of sorts. For years, it was the unofficial uniform of off-duty professional athletes, finance bros, and your dad — a garment prized primarily for its comfort and functionality. But more recently, it’s been embraced as a fashion statement (at least according to the kids on TikTok). Case in point: The J.Crew Heritage Cotton Quarter-Zip Sweater, a revival of one of the brand’s popular ’90s cotton sweaters, still feels contemporary. It layers effortlessly — under a spring jacket or over a button-up or white T-shirt — without giving office vibes (though it would be totally fine in an office). It’s made from soft, high-quality cotton, and its sturdy collar actually holds its shape. The ribbed cuffs and hem add a touch of polish. This quarter-zip sweater is soft, breathable, and built for layering. The midweight, 100% cotton knit feels soft yet substantial against the skin. It provides a nice amount of warmth in a slim silhouette, and it looks equally good over a T-shirt or a button-down or under a light jacket. It’s also low-maintenance: According to the label, this sweater can be machine-washed (on cold) and machine-dried (on low). When I followed those directions, there was no notable shrinkage. “It fits like a glove.” That’s how one tester described this sweater. And the design and fit are broadly appealing: It has a classic silhouette, a high neck with a roughly 8-inch zipper, and ribbing at the cuffs and hem. “Quarter-zips in general give me a Peyton Manning vibe, but this one is a bit less performance-y,” said one tester, who is 5-foot-11 and tested it in a size M. The sweater comes in sizes XS to XXL and in several versatile colors, including Navy (which I tested), Dark Cherry, and Carbon gray. And we found it ran true to size: I’m 6-foot-3 and wore a size L, which fit perfectly. The collar actually stands up. This is a small but important detail, and it separates a well-made quarter-zip top from a mediocre one. Many collars in this category are flimsy (including the one on the other quarter-zip shirt we tested, the Polo Ralph Lauren Luxury Jersey Quarter-Zip Pullover), and they fold over when unzipped (which I think kills the look). I prefer a stiff collar that stands up and gives off a kind of popped-jacket-collar vibe. This sweater’s collar holds its shape whether it’s zipped up or not. (And the collar is handy in cooler temps: The higher you zip it, the warmer the sweater gets.) Flaws but not dealbreakers The cotton is a bit thick for warmer weather. That’s a good thing overall, but it also means the sweater probably won’t work well in the summer. Key specs - Sizes: XS to XXL - Materials: 100% cotton - Colors: 13 A simple cotton shirt for lots of bodies: J.Crew Classic Piqué Polo Shirt Top pick This no-frills shirt comes in three cuts, so it suits a wide range of heights and builds. (Oddly, it’s available in only three colors.) The piqué cotton fabric feels slightly stiff at first, but it softens over time. J.Crew’s Classic Piqué Polo Shirt isn’t trying to reinvent the wheel, and that’s a big part of its appeal. This medium-weight cotton shirt is a nod to those worn on tennis courts in the 1930s, with a subtle piqué texture and signature details that have made the polo a wardrobe staple for decades. It comes in three cuts, so people of different heights and builds can find one that works. This polo looks more expensive than it is, and it’s often on sale. This is an old-school, by-the-book polo shirt. The design is clean and classic, and the self-fabric ribbed collar is stiff enough to be worn up or down. The shirt has a two-button placket, set-in sleeves, and a small tennis tail, which works nicely tucked or untucked. (An extended hem on the back of the shirt, a tennis tail was originally designed to keep a shirt tucked in while the wearer was playing tennis.) There’s no logo to speak of (although you can monogram it for $10), and for the logo-averse, that’s an advantage over our other short-sleeve polo pick, Polo Ralph Lauren’s The Iconic Mesh Polo Shirt. Depending on how you style this polo, it can skew preppy, sporty, or just put-together. “It’s very understated, but still looks nice,” one tester said. The Classic Piqué Polo is a great office-to-dinner shirt that works well with jeans, chinos, shorts, and pretty much anything else. The downside is the limited color selection: White, Navy, and Black. The shirt comes in three cuts, so it can suit different builds. It’s available in Classic, Slim, and Tall (in sizes XS to XXL), so it can work for a variety of body types. I tested the Classic fit in a size L. I’m 6-foot-3 and have an athletic build, and the shirt sat comfortably across my shoulders, with little room in the chest and a gentle taper through the torso (which I found flattering and non-clingy); the sleeves were snug without being restrictive. Another tester, who is 5-foot-11 and slender, tested the Classic fit in M (his usual size) and found the cut a tad too billowy: “A slim fit probably would have been a better profile,” he said. It looks more expensive than it is. The Classic Piqué Polo is made from cotton that’s U.S. Cotton Trust Protocol–certified (this certification tracks sustainability and supply chain). The piqué material’s waffle-like texture feels comfortably sturdy — the kind of fabric that should last a while and get softer with age. It’s not quite as soft as the Polo Ralph Lauren shirt, and it’s slightly thicker, but it’s typically about $40 cheaper. At the time of writing, J.Crew had it marked down to under $50; at that price, you could buy two colors for less than the cost of one Polo Ralph Lauren shirt. Flaws but not dealbreakers The color selection is limited. The options are White, Navy, and Black. Key specs - Sizes: Classic (XS to XXL), Slim (XS to XL), Tall (M to XXL) - Material: cotton piqué - Colors: three The king of polos: Polo Ralph Lauren The Iconic Mesh Polo Shirt and Polo Ralph Lauren Mesh Long-Sleeve Polo Shirt Top pick Made from a subtly textured cotton mesh weave, this classic delivers on its designer pedigree: It’s stylish, breathable, and comfortable. It comes in over 50 colors and multiple fits (including Big & Tall). But it’s pricey, and the logo can be polarizing. Polo Ralph Lauren’s The Iconic Mesh Polo Shirt and Mesh Long-Sleeve Polo Shirt have set the standard for polo shirts since the brand first introduced them, in 1972. “I finally understand why these are basically synonymous with the term polo,” one tester said. “It feels easily dressed-up or dressed-down, and a cut above the others I’ve worn.” The breathable cotton mesh material is cool and comfortable: It’s smoother, lighter, and less nubby than traditional piqué. The short-sleeve version is a warm-weather staple; the long-sleeve style offers that same breathable texture along with a little more coverage for cooler temps and casual layering. There’s a reason these shirts are considered the polo shirts. Although Ralph Lauren didn’t invent the polo shirt — that honor goes to René Lacoste — it has long been the standard-bearer. Ever since the debut of Polo Ralph Lauren shirts, more than 50 years ago, they have embodied a preppy, aspirational vibe, but not in a stuffy way: They’re intended to look casual and effortless, and they break in over time. The classic cotton mesh shirt — available with short or long sleeves — is familiar, versatile, and genuinely comfortable. The waffle-like weave creates tiny air pockets between the fabric and skin, so it’s more breathable than a jersey knit. It’s made from ring-spun combed cotton — a fine, smooth yarn without the scratchy fibers found in cheaper materials. These shirts come in tons of colors. The short-sleeve version is available in a whopping 54 colors, while the long-sleeve version comes in seven. And the colors strike different vibes. For example, the dark-gray Barclay Heather (with bright green logo) and the Polo Black (with red logo) connote casual office Fridays, whereas the White (with navy logo) and Baja Pink (with baby-blue logo) both bring pure summer vibes. I tested the Heritage Royal color, a vibrant royal blue with a red logo, and I liked it — until I went to a restaurant in San Juan, Puerto Rico, and noticed the staff members were all wearing the shirts, in the same color, as a uniform. (Next time I’ll go for the more subdued Parchment Cream.) They also come in multiple fits. In standard sizes (XS to XXL), the short-sleeve Iconic Mesh Polo is available in three cuts: Classic, Custom Slim, and Slim. The Classic cut is the roomiest, providing a fuller body, lower armholes, and longer sleeves; the Custom Slim cut has a trimmer waist and sleeves, but it’s only slightly slimmer across the body; and the Slim cut is fitted through the chest, back, and waist, with biceps-hugging sleeves. The short-sleeve style also comes in Big & Tall sizes, from 2X Big to 5X Big and M Tall to 4L Tall. (The long-sleeve style has fewer options: It comes in Classic and Custom Slim fits only, in sizes XS to XXL.) I’m 6-foot-3, and I tested the shirt in the Classic fit in a size L. The fit was fairly comfortable, but in the future I may try an XL for a more relaxed look, since I prefer to wear roomier clothing in the summer. Another tester, who is 5-foot-11 and slender, tested the shirt in the Classic fit in his usual size, M, and said it fit perfectly. You can wear these shirts with almost anything. The shirts slot right into a spring/summer wardrobe: They go with jeans, chinos, shorts, and even some dress trousers. The tennis tail in back works equally well tucked or untucked. Flaws but not dealbreakers Some people may find the neckline too restrictive. This shirt has a two-button placket, which felt unusually high and tight on my neck, even when it was fully unbuttoned. I was the only tester who had this issue, though, and I couldn’t find similar complaints online, so it may come down to personal preference. (Our J.Crew Classic Piqué Polo Shirt pick also has a two-button placket, but that one didn’t bother me.) It’s not for the logo-averse. We’re not typically pro-logo either, but we gave this one a pass because it’s an embroidered polo player. Key specs - Sizes: XS to XXL, in Classic, Custom Slim, and Slim fits (The Iconic Mesh Polo Shirt); XS to XXL, in Classic and Custom Slim fits (Mesh Long-Sleeve Polo Shirt); 2X to 5X and L Tall to 4L Tall (The Iconic Mesh Polo Shirt in Big & Tall) - Material: 100% cotton - Colors: over 50 (The Iconic Mesh Polo Shirt), 11 (Mesh Long-Sleeve Polo Shirt); 10 (The Iconic Mesh Polo Shirt in Big & Tall) Why you should trust us I am a writer covering style and accessories for Wirecutter. I’m the author of our guides to the best men’s suits, the best pants for the office (and beyond), and the best white T-shirts, among others. I’ve written about style and many other topics for publications including The New York Times Magazine, GQ, and Esquire. And I have an almost bank-breaking obsession with menswear. For this guide to the best men’s lightweight knits, sweaters, and polos, I did the following things: - I researched nearly 100 garments. - I enlisted two colleagues, with different body types and tastes, to do additional testing on the garments. - To immerse myself in the category, I spent a full day making the rounds to roughly a dozen stores in New York City — including Banana Republic, Buck Mason, J.Crew, and Uniqlo — and tried on various knitwear. Like all Wirecutter journalists, I review and test products with complete editorial independence. I’m never made aware of any business implications of my editorial recommendations. Read more about our editorial standards. How we picked and tested For this guide, we focused on lightweight knits. These are the pieces that will see you through milder weather and the transitional seasons: winter to spring, spring to summer, and summer to fall. We excluded anything that was too bulky or warm, as well as items in categories that already have their own dedicated guides (such as sweatshirts and cashmere sweaters). In the end, we decided to focus on a variety of knits made from cotton, merino wool, and related blends. We tested lightweight sweaters in various styles — including crewnecks, quarter-necks, and polos — along with classic short- and long-sleeve polo shirts. We sought versatile workhorse items that could be dressed up or down — the kind you’d wear to go to the office, run errands, or meet a friend for dinner. After compiling a (huge) initial list, I chose 24 garments to test myself. After I’d identified the most promising styles, I recruited two colleagues to test nine of the finalists. (One tester is 5-foot-11 and wears a size M; the other is 5-foot-7 and also wears a size M.) Their detailed feedback helped to inform our picks. To assess how this knitwear would fare in the wild, I wore each contender for at least a day (and usually more), and I experimented with different outfit and shoe combinations. I washed and dried each piece according to the labels, checking for shrinkage or other changes post-laundering. (Personally, I’m a stickler for following care instructions. And I recommend that you do the same, so your clothing has a longer life.) During testing, I spent nearly four weeks in New Orleans in March. It proved to be an interesting testing ground for lightweight knits. The temperature swung from the low 40s (Fahrenheit) to the high 70s. I also spent many hours indoors in institutional AC, which required layering. And many of the garments recommended in this guide proved indispensable. We made our picks based on the following criteria: Style: We looked for versatile pieces that would have broad appeal across many tastes and preferences. We wanted to find sweaters and polos that felt both modern and timeless — and that wouldn’t go out of style anytime soon. Fit: We searched for garments that would accommodate a range of body types. And we gave bonus points to items that came in a range of sizes and fits. Fabric: Nobody wants to throw on a garment that feels rough and itchy or that doesn’t breathe when it gets warmer outside. We focused on polos made with comfortable, high-quality knit fabric — mostly cotton or merino wool — that didn’t need special pampering to launder and maintain. Quality and construction: We considered the craftsmanship of each garment, examining the construction and details (such as ribbed cuffs and hems). Value: We tested items ranging from $60 to $275. As always, we were on the hunt for pieces that are made to last and worth every dollar. Other lightweight men’s knits worth considering If you want a super-lightweight merino sweater: The Proper Cloth Easy Care Italian Merino Crewneck Sweater (sizes XS to XXL) is so lightweight that it can feel like wearing a long-sleeve T-shirt. It’s made from 100% merino wool from Italy that’s soft and low-maintenance. (You can machine-wash this sweater on cold and even tumble-dry it on low.) I loved the slim, athletic fit. But it’s a little too pricey for what it is, especially compared with our similar (and much less expensive) Banana Republic Merino Crew-Neck Sweater pick. If you’re seeking a classic spring/summer cotton cable-knit: The Polo Ralph Lauren Cable-Knit Cotton Sweater is the quintessential Ralph Lauren sweater, and that’s its main draw. (For some, though, this could be the main drawback.) The textured, dimensional cable-knit and the iconic logo embroidered on the chest are instantly recognizable. This sweater is also very comfortable; made from 100% cotton, it feels soft and light against the skin and is just the right weight for a breezy morning walk on the beach. This crewneck has a standard fit, so it’s neither too slim nor too baggy, with rib-knit cuffs and hem. (It comes in sizes XS to XXL, and it’s sometimes available in Big & Tall sizes.) Style-wise, it matches nicely with jeans, chinos, and other casual pants; if you want to lean into the preppy look, this top can be layered over an oxford shirt. If you’re looking for an outrageously comfortable quarter-zip option: The Polo Ralph Lauren Luxury Jersey Quarter-Zip Pullover (sizes XS to XXL) makes you look like you’re properly dressed in a nice, lightweight sweater, yet it has the feel of a Sunday sweatshirt. The cotton-blend fabric (a smooth, lightweight mix of 69% cotton, 29% viscose, and 2% nylon) is “exceptionally comfortable,” according to one tester. I found myself reaching for this shirt in the spring, when I wanted a comfy extra layer both indoors and outdoors. This quarter-zip comes in about a dozen appealing colors (though a bit more variety would be nice). But the collar is annoyingly limp — the thin fabric doesn’t have enough structure to stand upright, unless it’s fully zipped. And the price (around $135) seemed a little high, though select colors do go on sale. If you want to splurge on a luxe cotton crewneck: For an everyday treat, the Todd Snyder Beechwood Crewneck Sweater (sizes XS to XXL) is an amazingly soft, good-looking sweater. It’s made from a notably lightweight organic cotton yarn that, according to the brand, has been specially spun to help it stay airy and hold its shape. The sweater is more elevated than a basic cotton crewneck. And it has interesting details, including raglan sleeves (which give it a sporty look) and a half-cardigan stitch (this knitting technique is characterized by a ribbed structure that gives the garment subtle texture). But it comes in just one color, Bisque (an easily stainable shade), and the price (around $250) is pretty steep for a cotton sweater. The competition Cotton polo shirts I have fond memories of Lacoste polos from the 1990s and early 2000s, and I’m an avid seeker of the brand’s vintagewear. But I was disappointed with the (short-sleeve) Lacoste Men’s Classic Fit Original L.12.12 Polo and Lacoste Men’s Classic Fit Long Sleeve L.12.12 Polo. The cotton was stiff and thin, and the fit was boxy; these shirts just weren’t worth the price. We tested the Lululemon Evolution Short-Sleeve Polo Shirt, thinking it would be nice to have a sportier polo in the mix. This shirt may be great on the golf course, but we didn’t love the sweat-wicking synthetic fabric (85% polyester, 10% lyocell, 5% Lycra), and the fit was too slim. If you’re on a tighter budget, the Gap Pique Polo Shirt and Quince Organic Cotton Long Sleeve Pique Polo are two perfectly adequate options. But they couldn’t compete with our J.Crew and Polo Ralph Lauren cotton polo picks. The Gap shirt had a too-tight fit, while the Quince one was slightly itchy against the skin. Sweaters The Reigning Champ Lightweight Merino Harry Cardigan seemed a little cheap and thin. At the time of writing, the brand was updating this style (and stock is already running low). Because we’ve been impressed by some of this brand’s other offerings, we’re looking forward to checking out the new model. The Quince Organic Cotton-Silk Pique Crewneck Sweater was soft to the touch. But the weave was so loose that it seemed as if this one wouldn’t hold its shape for long. The Quince 100% Organic Cotton Ribbed Crewneck Sweater, meanwhile, is slightly heavier than we’d prefer for warmer months, and it didn’t feel as luxurious as the other cotton pieces we recommend. The Buck Mason Seafarer Cotton Rib Cardigan is made from 100% cotton, and we thought it felt great. The design is kind of bland, however, and this one didn’t seem worth the price (over $200). The Suitsupply Cotton Silk Crewneck was way too slim and short. On my 6-foot-3 frame, the sweater (in a size L) squeezed my chest and belly, and it landed above my belt line.
